subject.title: feat(cron): serve cron run history from the task ledger

question: Should this PR complete the upgrade-safe retention and migration boundary before flipping cron history reads, or be narrowed to write-only staging for a later migration PR?
rationale: The permanent ownership direction is reasonable, but choosing when reads become authoritative determines whether existing history, startup availability, and stale-run recovery can regress during upgrades.

options.title: Complete upgrade safety first
options.body: Add equivalent per-source retention, move persistent import to the explicit migration or doctor owner, reconcile thin mirrors, and prove stale-run recovery before switching reads.

options.title: Narrow to write staging
options.body: Keep legacy reads authoritative and land only full-fidelity ledger writes plus compatible schema support, deferring the read flip to the migration PR.

options.title: Accept staged rollout risk
options.body: Land the current read flip with explicit ownership of shortened retention, duplicate mirrors, startup import cost, and recovery mismatches.

recommendation.title: Complete upgrade safety first
recommendation.body: Add equivalent per-source retention, move persistent import to the explicit migration or doctor owner, reconcile thin mirrors, and prove stale-run recovery before switching reads.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision primarily governs the task-ledger persistence and lifecycle contract that their recent feature history most closely owns.
